name: Generative Concepts
tagline: Generates and costs every viable concept for the site and the brief, so the best one is chosen on evidence rather than habit.
problem: Concepts are compared on inconsistent bases, so the first idea studied is often the one built.
how: A project brief and site data
Generates layouts and costs every concept for capex, opex and returns
The concept with the best lifetime economics, chosen on one basis
features: Layouts from a brief: Arrangements, equipment lists and quantities generated for engineers to refine
Concept costing: Capital and operating cost for each concept from the cost model
Lifetime economics: Levelized cost and returns for every option, updated live
Trade-off comparison: Concepts ranked on cost, schedule, risk and returns
Alternatives library: Design and contracting alternatives, each priced against the project’s own packages
Outside-in check: The concept’s cost per unit of capacity against comparable plants, before it is chosen
Layout generator: Every arrangement enumerated from the site boundary, anchors and equipment envelopes, and screened against hard engineering checks
Rejection ledger: Every rejected option, with the check it failed

screens.title: Concept selection
screens.caption: Pick the development concept, such as a tension leg platform, and the export routes.

screens.title: Schematic and capital total
screens.caption: Build the facility from components and pipelines; the capital total updates as each piece is added.

notes: These two screens come from Costline, where the concept options and the schematic builder live. They show choosing among fourteen offshore concepts and assembling the chosen one from components.
